startup.name: a0.dev
startup.one_liner: We make mobile apps using AI.
startup.description: Platform that generates custom React Native projects so mobile developers build apps in days. The founders say they launched top ranking apps used by hundreds of thousands and now build tooling for faster development. Three person team in San Francisco.

yc_acceptance.basis: Starting prior is about 1 percent for a random applicant (0.6 to 2 percent range, references/yc_acceptance.md). Up for shipped consumer apps with hundreds of thousands of users, which show execution (real usage factor) and technical founders. Down because AI app generation is crowded and the pitch is vague about who pays. Net about 3 percent, conditional on the batch already given.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most likely say that AI generation of mobile apps is crowded and may be absorbed by general coding assistants, and that the founders' own consumer apps are a different business from the tool they now pitch. Without paying customers for the tool, partners may see a demo more than a company.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --tag 'Developer Tools' --years 2022-2025 --calibration-only: seed cond 55% (n=29, lower 50 / upper 59), series_a cond 38% (n=16), series_b 0% known (n=6, upper 9%). Broad cohort --industry B2B --years 2022-2025: seed 59% (n=126), series_a 26% (n=74), series_b 16% (n=19). Time table era 2022+: seed median 6 months, p75 14; series_a p25 19.4, median 28, p75 38 months from batch start.
anchors.adjustment_reason: Window is 22.4 months from 2025-01-06 to 2026-11-17 and the number is for a round above about 1M from outside investors inside that window, not ever. Anchor 0.55 for the developer tools tag and 0.59 for B2B; 0.52 is 0.95x of the tag anchor. A 22 month window covers more than the 2022 and later p75 time to seed of 14 months, so nearly all eventual seeds fit. Hot AI coding sector and strong consumer traction are not lifted above the anchor, per the winners test. These odds do not rank this company against others.

bands.rationale: Small post YC round under 3M, common for a three person developer tools team with traction from consumer apps.
Institutional seed near the 2022 and later median 4.1M.
Strong seed if the tool shows fast paid growth in the AI coding boom, near the quartile of 6.5M to 10M in recent press covered rounds.
Large round in the AI app builder category, where well known entrants raised big seeds; rare for three people.

ladder.why_it_fails: The seed step fails if the platform cannot convert free users into paid developers, if general tools such as coding assistants and larger app builders cover the same job, or if the founders go back to consumer apps. Draftbit reached only a seed over years, Namaste Business and Unflow shut down, and Expo and Thunkable show that mobile builders needed years to reach later rounds.

Draftbit never passed seed and Thunkable and Expo took years to B, so an early A would need a breakout in paid subscribers that the input does not yet show.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series C in under two years of YC would need a category winning position in AI coding, a market where Microsoft, Google and funded competitors are already scaling. No analog among mobile builders reached C quickly, and Expo took close to a decade to a larger round.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Most likely the product is overtaken by general AI coding tools and app builders and the team stalls or sells for a small sum, as with Namaste Business and Unflow. Upside needs a breakout among AI mobile builders, where distribution and model costs favor larger entrants. Expo shows the infrastructure route can reach later rounds but after years.

killers.risk: General coding assistants absorb app generation
killers.evidence: Coding assistants and large app builders already generate React Native apps; the market search lists many AI React Native builders such as RapidNative and Rork.
killers.mitigation: Own a niche such as native store ready apps with design quality.

killers.risk: Consumer apps are a different business
killers.evidence: The traction cited is from the founders own apps, not from the developer tool customers.
killers.mitigation: Show developers paying for the tool, not consumers for apps.

killers.risk: Low switching costs and thin pricing
killers.evidence: Output is code the user can export, and model costs are falling, so differentiation is thin.
killers.mitigation: Build workflow lock in via templates and integrations.

killers.evidence: A team of 3 must run apps and a platform while competitors raise large rounds.
killers.mitigation: Choose one product and hire early.

competition_now.name: RapidNative
competition_now.what: AI to React Native app builder with exportable code
competition_now.traction: Vendor ranking guides list it among leaders

competition_now.name: Natively and Bilt
competition_now.what: AI builders with app store deployment
competition_now.traction: Paid plans from about 25 dollars a month

technical_complexity.rationale: Generating a working React Native project is feasible with current models; the hard part is quality, store compliance and a build and preview loop. A small team can build the core in months, but staying ahead of model providers is difficult, so the moat is data on what ships to the stores.

takeover_risk.rationale: General coding assistants can add mobile templates quickly, and the search shows many funded AI app builders. Expo itself could add generation. This is among the highest takeover risks.

evidence.claim: Many vendors sell AI React Native builders and rank each other, showing real demand and a crowded field.
Pricing listings show paid plans from about 25 dollars a month with deployment included.

roadmap.goal: Prove developers pay for the tool.
actions: Launch the tool to a waitlist of mobile developers

roadmap.goal: Show retention and growth in paid subscriptions.
actions: Ship a differentiating workflow such as store submission
roadmap.proof: Monthly recurring revenue growing month on month with retained cohorts.

pros.evidence: The founders say their apps reached hundreds of thousands of users, evidence of execution.
Many AI app builder vendors and guides show active developer and buyer interest.

brand.name: a0.dev
brand.name_check: python3 -I scripts/name_features.py --score "a0.dev" --era 2022+: invented or proper name, 1 character detected, no descriptor.
strengths: The dot dev domain signals the audience
weaknesses: Hard to say aloud or search
brand.rationale: A domain style name is short but awkward to say, and cannot be searched easily. Such names are common in developer tools, but they do not add recall the way a pronounceable brand does.

narrative.headline: A fast moving founder team in the most crowded and absorbable corner of AI coding: seed is about even over 22 months, later rounds are unlikely in the window.
narrative.general_summary: a0.dev generates React Native apps with AI for mobile developers. The founders have real app traction but the tool business is unproven and competes with many funded builders and general coding assistants. The window is 22.4 months from 2025-01-06 to 2026-11-17, long enough for most seeds, so the seed odds sit near the developer tools anchor of 55 percent. Series A given seed is about 10 percent in the window. The odds do not rank this company against others.

assumptions: Blind forecast as of 2025-01-06 using only the input.
Seed means above about 1M from outside investors inside the 22.4 month window.
The AI app builder boom of 2025 is not assumed beyond what the input shows.
